coordinatorSummary: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Twelve attacks run, none landed. Custody is clean: e40fc2eb at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left a6081c6, file 08 at 6d593a11 and COORD at 20a8f69b with a clean tree, all six file pins plus the D-154 commit pin reproducing, and the gate table still at 28 rows. The entry records what it says it records. Its ten leftover EE ids set-compare equal to the artifact's, EE-3a is carried across with the discharged-by-DR-133 basis and no claim of naming, and the riding trio EE-6b, EE-7c and EE-7e keeps the disclaimer that they are not named at G09, G14 or G16 by this entry — which is the sentence that keeps the record honest, and the same one the dispatch attacks by name. My own join verdict is represented exactly at ACCEPT 0/0 with the advisory id included; the Codex half I confirmed only as a digest. Every dispatch prohibition is refused in terms, the readiness recital matches the live register on all three figures, required-now stays 24, and Decision 4 uses the 'Proposed later work' heading with a permissive body, with 'Owed later' occurring nowhere. One check specific to this row: it is where I previously accepted a false enforcement claim, so I looked for any characterisation of what G09 tests. The entry makes none — it records EE-6b as capable-of-riding without describing the property — so the honesty-not-confinement posture recorded in v5 and preserved in the join is neither restated nor disturbed. Two items are recorded as considered and declined, including that Decision 4's branch (b) omits the same-act naming structure D-146 and D-149 carried; branch (b) describes naming at obligations rather than adding rows, the artifact proposes no new rows, and branch (a) routes explicitly through a D-086 successor. After this entry, ten DR-117 EE classes remain leftover-design and three remain unnamed at the gates they could ride; DR-117 stays OPEN, not eligible in kind, not SATISFIED.
